overview: For regular player-versus-environment missions, this table chooses the next mission from risk-based groups with different chances.
description: Risk-qualified weighted pools that choose the next non-survival PvE mission from a row's candidate missions; each row defines both a pool weight and parallel candidate/weight arrays.

Id.simple: The name the game uses for this set of missions. The game remembers the last one it used and leaves it out next time.
Id.technical: Native FName; export metadata sets ImportKeyField=Id and the dump writes the key as ID, with all 223 exported row names unique and matching ID. GamePvE_PickMission does not find a lottery row by this member: it enumerates the loaded rows, then copies the chosen row's Id into the FName& LotteryId argument, which callers pass as FGamePvESettings::PickedLotteryId. FGamePvESettings::Reset initializes that cached id to NAME_None, and the settings copy assignment carries it; on a later non-survival pick a non-None value removes the lottery row whose Id matches before the pool is weighted.

Id_GlobalThreshold.simple: Which risk level this group of missions is meant for. You only draw from it when your current risk fits that range.
Id_GlobalThreshold.technical: Native FName with no explicit constructor initializer (NAME_None). After the early extra-mission cutoff, GamePvE_PickMission walks the lottery rows from the end and asks each UDataTable in GlobalThresholdDataTables (DTM+0x300), in array order, for a FGameDataTableRow_GlobalThreshold named this Id; the first table containing the row wins. A row is removed when no threshold row exists or when the cast int32 RiskValue is outside the inclusive [Min, Max] floats (InRange_FloatFloat with both endpoints included). All 223 exported rows use one of the 15 PVE_MISSION_A_01..PVE_MISSION_E_03 names; those rows resolve in GlobalThresholdDataTable and form contiguous integer bands from 0 to 50000. PVE_MISSION_X_0_99999 exists in that asset but is not referenced here; a risk outside 0..50000 therefore leaves no eligible row and the picker falls back to PVE_X_00 without updating LotteryId.

Weights.simple: How likely this group of missions is to be drawn compared with the other available groups. A bigger number gives it a better chance each time.
Weights.technical: float, constructor default 0.0f; all 223 exported rows instead set 1000.0. The value is a dimensionless relative weight, not a percent or normalized probability. After threshold filtering and exclusion of the row whose Id equals a non-None LotteryId, one Weights value per surviving row is passed in row order to GamePvE_PickWeightedIndex. That helper returns INDEX_NONE for an empty list; otherwise it sums the floats, rolls StoryFRand()*sum (StoryFRand is approximately [0,1)), returns the first index where the remaining roll is less than that weight after subtracting earlier weights, and returns the last index if no weight wins. With an all-zero sum the roll is zero and the last index is returned, so a zero-weight row is not inherently unpickable. When no row survives, GamePvE_PickMission returns PVE_X_00 and leaves LotteryId unchanged; otherwise it writes the selected row's Id to LotteryId before choosing a mission.

Id_PvEMission.simple: The missions the game can pick from this group. Blank places in the list do not offer a mission.
Id_PvEMission.technical: Native TArray<FName>, default empty. The selector walks these source indices, skips None, and builds a compressed weight list; after choosing a compressed index it returns Lottery->Id_PvEMission[Pick] directly rather than indexing a separate filtered id list. That reconstructed quirk would shift the result (possibly to a None slot) if a row ever placed None before a later non-None candidate. All 223 exported rows have 12 slots, with 2..12 non-None ids followed only by trailing None padding, so no supplied row triggers the shift; all 996 non-None ids are unique within and across rows and resolve in PvEMissionDataTable. If a row has no non-None candidate, the weighted helper returns INDEX_NONE and the picker returns the PVE_X_00 fallback.

MissionWeights.simple: How likely each mission in the group is to be picked. A bigger number helps, while a mission already played in this run gets much less.
MissionWeights.technical: Native TArray<float>, default empty; it must stay parallel to Id_PvEMission. For each non-None candidate at source index i the picker reads MissionWeights[i] with no length check, then multiplies by 0.01f once for every PreviousMissions entry equal to that id (repeated prior ids compound the penalty). The surviving values form a compressed parallel list for GamePvE_PickWeightedIndex; zero weights are still added and can be selected when no weight is positive. The export has 12 floats in every row, with 1000.0 at the 996 non-None ids and 0.0 at every None slot and no other values. The pick index is compressed but the returned id is direct-indexed, as documented under Id_PvEMission.

notes: Export coverage: the sole supplied PvEMissionLotteryDataTable asset has 223 rows with RowStruct GameDataTableRow_PvEMissionLottery and ImportKeyField=Id; no numbered or localized shards were supplied. Every row uses 15 risk-band threshold ids and 12-slot parallel id/weight arrays; all non-None candidate ids exist in PvEMissionDataTable.

Loader/cache trace: StartInitialLoading registers the PvEMissionLotteryDataTable loader, manager Tick resolves it into PvEMissionLotteryDataTables (DTM+0x910); thresholds come from GlobalThresholdDataTables (DTM+0x300). The returned mission id is subsequently resolved through PvEMissionDataTables (DTM+0x900) by GamePvE_FindMissionRow / GamePvE_GetMissionMapId and is used by wave and task picking. PickedLotteryId is cached in FGamePvESettings (Reset to NAME_None, copied with settings), not read from this table's asset metadata.

Caller conditions and precedence: GameMode==2 skips this table entirely and builds PVE_SURVIVAL_MISSION_%02d ids; status/verdicts.json confirms the retail format has no stray quotes (the nearby source comment is stale), and PVE_SURVIVAL_MISSION_01 is returned only if that generated id is missing. Otherwise, three or more already-played missions return PVE_EXTRA_MISSION_01 before any table access. Risk filtering runs before previous-lottery exclusion; if either leaves zero rows the picker returns PVE_X_00 and does not overwrite the cached LotteryId.

RiskValue is supplied by the caller: the offline interval and loopback beacon mock use the integer mean of FGamePvESettings::RiskValueArray, while the online host uses GamePvE_RiskSumModulo (the mean of SOS users' RiskValue, or all users when no SOS user exists). The picker compares that int32 as a float against the threshold rows' float bounds.

Evidence strength: GamePvE_PickMission 0x1306610 is marked behavioural in status/functions.json (BEHAV-certified, not byte-matched); the risk-class helper 0x1305fa0 and mission finder 0x12fb320 are also behavioural. Field names and runtime comments come from the local C++ reconstruction, while row counts, values and foreign-key relationships are observations from the supplied cooked-data exports. No retail Blueprint bytecode was inspected, and the source/content snapshot is partial, so additional retail-only wiring is not asserted.

The direct source-index return after skipping None ids is a property of the reconstructed consumer. It is visible in the supplied source; the exported rows' None padding is trailing only, so the quirk is a data-editing hazard rather than a demonstrated shift in the shipped export.

usages.detail: Resolves the PvEMissionLotteryDataTable loader into PvEMissionLotteryDataTables (DTM+0x910) after all table loads complete.
GamePvE_PickMission is the only traced direct consumer: survival bypass, extra-mission cutoff, risk filtering, previous-lottery exclusion, and both weighted picks.
Resolves Id_GlobalThreshold in GlobalThresholdDataTables in table order and applies the inclusive Min/Max risk test.
Removes the row whose Id equals the cached non-None LotteryId so the same pool is not picked twice consecutively.
Builds the row-level Weights list and writes the chosen row's Id back to the FName& LotteryId output.
Builds compressed candidate weights from parallel MissionWeights, skipping None ids and applying 0.01f per matching previously played mission.
Returns the picked mission from the original Id_PvEMission array using the compressed pick index; PVE_X_00 is returned when the pick list is empty.
Offline interval computes the mean RiskValueArray and calls the picker with PvESettings.PvEMissionIds and PickedLotteryId; the result feeds map, wave, and task selection.
Online host computes GamePvE_RiskSumModulo and runs the same picker on host-side PvESettings, updating the interval status.
Loopback beacon mock uses the mean RiskValueArray and the same picker before propagating the online interval status.
Downstream cache: the picked mission id is resolved in PvEMissionDataTables by GamePvE_GetMissionMapId; mission finder 0x12fb320 filters that same table by row type.
